ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that in the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$, the graph of the linear function $y=kx+b(k\ne 0)$ passes through points A and $B(-1,0)$, the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{6}{x}$ also passes through point A, and the abscissa of point A is 2. Point C is a point on the positive half of the x-axis, connect $AC$, $\tan\angle ACB=\frac{3}{4}$. A line through point C is drawn perpendicular to the x-axis and intersects the graphs of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{6}{x}$ and the linear function $y=kx+b(k\ne 0)$ at points D and E, respectively. Find the coordinates of points D and E.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw $AH \perp x$-axis at point H.

$\therefore \tan\angle ACB = \frac{AH}{CH} = \frac{3}{4}$.

$\because A(2,3)$,

$\therefore AH=3$, $OH=2$

$\therefore CH=4$,

$\therefore OC=OH+CH=6$,

$\therefore C(6,0)$.

$\because x_C=x_D=x_E=6$.

$\therefore y_D=\frac{6}{x_D}=1$, $y_E=x_E+1=7$,

$\therefore D(6,1)$, $E(6,7)$;

Hence, the coordinates of points D and E are $D=\boxed{(6,1)}$, $E=\boxed{(6,7)}$.

In right triangle AHC, the angle at C is the same angle made by AC with the x-axis, so tan∠ACB=AH/CH=3/4. Since AH=3, get CH=4, and since H has x-coordinate 2, C has x-coordinate 2+4=6. Then the vertical through C gives x_D=x_E=6. Compute D from the hyperbola: y=6/6=1. Determine the straight line through A(2,3) and B(-1,0), giving slope 1 and equation y=x+1, so at x=6, y=7. Thus D=(6,1), E=(6,7).

推理：点 A 的横坐标为 2，且 A 在反比例函数 y=6/x 上，所以 A=(2,6/2)=(2,3)。设 C=(c,0)。由图可知 C 在 A 的右侧，所以 c>2。因为 CB 沿 x 轴向左，CA 从 C 指向 A 的水平距离为 c-2，竖直高度为 3，所以 tan∠ACB=3/(c-2)。已知 tan∠ACB=3/4，因此 3/(c-2)=3/4，解得 c-2=4，即 c=6，所以 C=(6,0)。一次函数经过 A(2,3) 和 B(-1,0)，斜率为 (3-0)/(2-(-1))=1，因此直线方程为 y=x+1。过 C 的竖直线为 x=6，所以 D 在 y=6/x 上，D=(6,6/6)=(6,1)；E 在 y=x+1 上，E=(6,6+1)=(6,7)。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This method avoids constructing an auxiliary foot explicitly and instead parameterizes C as an unknown coordinate, using vectors/horizontal and vertical differences to express tan∠ACB directly.
planner_metadata.image_role: Use the image to confirm C lies to the right of A and B on the x-axis, so c>2 and the horizontal distance in the angle formula is c-2; also use the image to see D and E lie on the same vertical line through C.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the text facts that A is on y=6/x with abscissa 2, B=(-1,0), tan∠ACB=3/4, and D/E are intersections of the vertical through C with the inverse proportional and linear graphs respectively.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Apply analytic geometry: represent unknown point C=(c,0), compute tangent of an angle against a horizontal ray as rise/run, derive a two-point line equation, and evaluate functions at a fixed x-coordinate.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, it is known that in the Cartesian coordinate system $xOy$, the graph of the linear function $y=kx+b(k\ne 0)$ passes through points A and $B(-1,0)$, the graph of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{6}{x}$ also passes through point A, and the abscissa of point A is 2. Point C is a point on the positive half of the x-axis, connect $AC$, $\tan\angle ACB=\frac{3}{4}$. A line through point C is drawn perpendicular to the x-axis and intersects the graphs of the inverse proportion function $y=\frac{6}{x}$ and the linear function $y=kx+b(k\ne 0)$ at points D and E, respectively. Find the coordinates of points D and E.
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw $AH \perp x$-axis at point H.

$\therefore \tan\angle ACB = \frac{AH}{CH} = \frac{3}{4}$.

$\because A(2,3)$,

$\therefore AH=3$, $OH=2$

$\therefore CH=4$,

$\therefore OC=OH+CH=6$,

$\therefore C(6,0)$.

$\because x_C=x_D=x_E=6$.

$\therefore y_D=\frac{6}{x_D}=1$, $y_E=x_E+1=7$,

$\therefore D(6,1)$, $E(6,7)$;

Hence, the coordinates of points D and E are $D=\boxed{(6,1)}$, $E=\boxed{(6,7)}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a rectangular coordinate system xOy, a straight line rises toward the upper right, and passes through point B on the left side of the x-axis and point A in the first quadrant; an inverse proportional function curve decreases in the first quadrant, and also passes through point A. Point C is located on the positive semi-axis of the x-axis and is to the lower right of A, and line segment AC has been connected. Through C a vertical line is drawn, and this vertical line intersects the inverse proportional curve at the lower point D, and intersects the rising straight line at the higher point E. Reasoning: The abscissa of A is 2, and A is on y=6/x, so A=(2,3). Suppose A makes a perpendicular to the x-axis, with foot H, then AH=3, and the abscissa of H is 2. Because B and C are on the x-axis, ∠ACB is consistent with the angle formed by AC and the x-axis. In right triangle AHC, tan∠ACB=AH/CH=3/4. From AH=3, CH=4 is obtained, therefore the abscissa of C is 2+4=6, namely C=(6,0). The vertical line through C makes the abscissas of D and E both 6. D is on y=6/x, so y_D=6/6=1, D=(6,1). The straight line passes through A(2,3) and B(-1,0), and its slope is (3-0)/(2-(-1))=1, so its equation is y=x+1; when x=6, y_E=7, so E=(6,7).
